failures.injected_rule: When defining metrics for an empirical study involving game agents, verify that each metric provides a necessary gradient of measurement relative to the thesis claim; specifically, when evaluating against an optimal opponent in a solved game, discard metrics that are constant (like draw rate) and prioritize those that vary with agent quality or efficiency, because static baselines do not distinguish learner competence. Additionally, ensure that any visualisation requirement (e.g., learning curves) is structurally supported by the data pipeline in the same cycle; if the experimental module only outputs aggregated final stats, explicitly add a training log mechanism to the experimental plan rather than assuming the figures module can infer temporal dynamics from static output.

When defining an interface that returns auxiliary data structures (such as `info` dicts in RL environments), the outline must explicitly declare both the schema of the return tuple and the contents of any nested dictionaries, because consumers depend on this structural contract for safe usage.

rules.rule: When synthesizing an experimental baseline that must serve as a comparative reference, ensure it is an independent agent or strategy distinct from the training opponent, and verify that the declared evaluation metrics explicitly include any composite success criteria mentioned in the prompt (e.g., combining wins and draws) to avoid logical gaps.

When defining metrics for an empirical study involving game agents, verify that each metric provides a necessary gradient of measurement relative to the thesis claim; specifically, when evaluating against an optimal opponent in a solved game, discard metrics that are constant (like draw rate) and prioritize those that vary with agent quality or efficiency, because static baselines do not distinguish learner competence. Additionally, ensure that any visualisation requirement (e.g., learning curves) is structurally supported by the data pipeline in the same cycle; if the experimental module only outputs aggregated final stats, explicitly add a training log mechanism to the experimental plan rather than assuming the figures module can infer temporal dynamics from static output.

When defining an interface that returns auxiliary data structures (such as `info` dicts in RL environments), the outline must explicitly declare both the schema of the return tuple and the contents of any nested dictionaries, because consumers depend on this structural contract for safe usage.

When defining an experimental pipeline that requires baseline comparisons, explicitly document the evaluation of all comparative agents (including self-play or agent-vs-identical-agent) and their corresponding output records in the CSV interface before finalizing the plan, because visualizations depend on the presence of these specific data rows which are not implicitly generated by training logs.
